licences.notes: Words as printed in the Peters vocal score: the broken words with the print's ellipses, Sii, dì, bell' idol, and Don Alfonso's aside in brackets. The first bar's -fanno, the end of the sisters' Muojo d'affanno from the recitative before, is sung here but belongs to that recitative's line.

licences.source: Edition Peters vocal score (Edition Peters Nr. 4474, plate 11446, edited by Georg Schünemann), pages 56–62, bars 1–53 of No. 9
licences.author: Kurt Soldan (1891–1946), piano reduction
licences.notes: Written out from the printed pages: sung lines and piano each read by two independent readers, every disagreement settled on the page by a judge (in two page ranges, pp. 56–59 and 60–62), a separate sweep for dynamics and other marks, then checked bar by bar by two fresh checkers (one error found in bar 8, a left-hand F sharp, and corrected; the chorus clean). The German singing translation is left out, and handwritten pencil marks on p. 57 are ignored. Bar 1 begins with the sisters' -fanno, the end of the recitative before. Bar 27, the last Andante bar, is printed with three quarters before the double bar and is set as 3/4; bar 28 is the chorus's one-quarter upbeat, set as 1/4. Each soloist and each chorus part has its own staff; the sopranos and altos share one staff in the print and are written as two parts (where one notehead serves both, both sing it). One printed slur that crosses from the right hand to the left hand in bars 7–8 cannot be encoded and is left out. Playback tempo: Andante, played at ♩ = 53, then the chorus Maestoso at a half note = 67 (♩ = 134, the pace of “Bella vita militar”); about 2¾ minutes in all, from the median lengths of five recordings (Böhm, Haitink, Solti, Nézet-Séguin, Currentzis); Mozart gives the words only.
